expert.by: Claude (single session, written from the syllabus line and the fetched sources before storyboarding; not independent of the builder, so a later owner review should repeat it)

items.item: This topic has a real hands-on lab (lab/shop_dbt/, examples.py): a full dbt-core project (seeds, three staging models, two mart models, a Jinja macro, thirteen data tests, one unit test, one exposure) was built and run against a local DuckDB target, with no packaging workaround needed (unlike the previous topic's MetricFlow install)

at.step: Reveal: the lab — ref(), not table names

items.item: The DAG shown in the reel and in examples.py is read directly from the real project's own target/manifest.json after a real dbt build (lab/manifest-dag.json is a frozen snapshot of that field), not drawn from imagination

at.step: Reveal: the lab — the DAG, read from dbt's own manifest

items.item: The second predict's reveal (the lab's failing data test) is backed by an actually executed failure: a dangling customer_id was introduced into the seed data, dbt build genuinely failed the relationships test and SKIPped fct_orders, mart_revenue_by_region, and the exposure, and the row was then reverted and the build re-verified clean

at.step: Reveal: the lab — a failing data test actually blocking downstream models

items.item: The closing "Prove it" scenario is a genuinely new, independently executed test, not merely asserted: a model selecting from a staging model's literal table name instead of ref() was added temporarily and built with eight threads against a freshly emptied database, and it failed for real with a missing-table error because dbt had no dependency edge to schedule it after its real dependency

at.step: Prove it

items.item: The unit test is run in isolation (dbt test --select test_type:unit) to show concretely that it validates the macro's own compiled logic against two fabricated rows, without ever touching the seeded data — distinguishing it from a data test in the reel's own words, not just in the source quote

at.step: Reveal: the unit test, run in isolation, no seeded data touched

items.item: dbt Mesh's cross-project refs, model contracts, versions and access levels are deliberately not built hands-on, since cross-project ref() requires an Enterprise or Enterprise+ plan and a second project that this session's single local DuckDB project cannot stand up — disclosed explicitly in SOURCES.md rather than silently implied to have been tested

at.step: Reveal: docs and lineage; dbt Mesh, named and sourced

items.item: The first predict (step three) is red-teamed against the plausible wrong answer that dbt can infer a dependency from any SQL referencing another table's name; the Prove-It scenario at the end independently re-confirms the same mistake with a real build failure, not just a restated claim
